walkthroughs.body_html:
What is Business? — a core area of A-Level Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

What is Business? brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with What is Business?.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Porter's three generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
options: Diversification
Focus
Innovation
Acquisition

mcqs.q: The 'Blue Ocean' concept was proposed by:
options: Porter
Kim and Mauborgne
Hamel and Prahalad
Drucker
Productivity is the total amount produced by a business.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.
Output per unit of input (per worker, per hour) — measuring efficiency, not total output. A small efficient firm can be more productive than a large inefficient one.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.

mcqs.q: What is operations management concerned with?
options: Operations management is the same as general management.
The design and control of the production process and business operations — converting inputs into outputs efficiently. It includes capacity, quality, supply chain, and process improvement.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.
Operations management is only about manufacturing factories.

mcqs.q: Why are cash flow and profit different on different time-scales?
options: Cash flow only matters at year-end.
Cash flow and profit are the same thing measured differently.
Productivity is the number of employees a business has.

Profit is recognised when a sale is made (even on credit); cash flow is when money actually moves. A profitable sale today may produce no cash for 60 days while bills are due — creating a cash-flow problem despite profit.
